answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a fixed deposit of tokens before it may submit jobs or claim rewards, then slash that deposit when independent audits prove fraud. This makes Sybil attacks costly: inventing a thousand hollow personas requires a thousand funded deposits, not merely a script that can mint names. The deposit should be large enough to outweigh expected gains, while honest agents can recover it after a delay. Calling the audit ledger jade or timber changes nothing; the deterrent is capital at risk, not identity labels.
